analysis.title: GS Global Equities Call 5 Nov 2026
key_insights: US futures mixed pre-market: SPX +20bps, NDX -45bps, RTY +65bps, UST 10yr -0.5bps at 4.88%, WTI +1.5% at $89.50. Semis, data centers and AI infrastructure keep underperforming in a post-election rotation and broadening rally. WTI is down 14% on the week.
Pre-market semis weakness: SMH -2%, DRAM -4%, Neoclouds -2 to -3%, VRT -2.5%, Hynix -9%, Samsung -7.5%, Tokyo Electron -9%. QCOM (-9% pre-market) and ARM (-4%) prints underwhelmed.

31 baskets on the GS US 1D Macro monitor had a move above 3 sigma yesterday. GS compares the volatility to the US-China tariff shock, DeepSeek, Liberation Day and the 2024 election. NDX outperformed Semis (SOX) by nearly 460 bps, a top-10 daily spread in 10+ years.
Breadth has improved: about 72% of SPX names are above their 50-day moving average, up from about 21% on Sept 30 and the highest level YTD against a YTD average of 53%.
The desk's biggest theme yesterday was demand for hyperscalers and supply in semis. The desk did not see chasing in consumer or financials.
Treasury 4Q26 borrowing estimate is $618bn vs GS projection of $571bn. The 1Q27 estimate is $800bn vs GS $713bn, driven by a higher TGA cash balance target of $1tn.

Treasury kept nominal coupon, TIPS and FRN auction sizes unchanged but removed 'at least' from its guidance that sizes stay in place for 'at least the next several quarters'. GS now expects auction size increases to begin in August 2027.

Treasury expects $70bn of liquidity buybacks this quarter. The 7-year note moves to a quarterly new issue cycle starting in March, with GS expecting auction sizes of $46bn / $43bn / $43bn through the quarter. TBAC noted signs of increasing price sensitivity for bills amid sluggish MMF AUM growth.
Retail group rose 5.5% yesterday, its biggest 1-day move in a year and +390 bps vs SPY, the 2nd largest 1-day outperformance in 2 years. XRT is at 5-year highs and XLP is at all-time highs.

Feiler sees a lack of conviction in the consumer rally, with client inbounds mostly asking 'what can I fade?', concentrated in Staples but also in Discretionary. High-touch and PB desks have not seen aggressive single-stock buying. Discretionary and Staples are at multi-year lows as a share of the GS PB book and long/short ratios are just off the lows. Supply has largely dried up.
Interest in low-income consumer names rose on debate over whether SNAP and Medicaid headwinds ease in mid-2027 around debt limit negotiations, along with lower oil.
GS Macro's consumer dashboard is titled 'Resilience'. GS forecasts near-potential spending growth in 2027 and real income growth acceleration in 2027, particularly for the lowest-income consumers.

Callahan: NDX futures rallied about 400 bps from overnight lows. Semis are further below their 200-day moving average, with INTC, CBRS, MRVL, TER, CAT and FFIV in oversold territory. Client conversations focus on the magnitude of moves rather than direction, and on whether the market over-prices policy outcomes (CSPs > Semis, drawdowns in IPPs or E&Cs, rally in consumer discretionary).
Semiconductor forward multiples compressed more than 40% over two months, from 28x to 16x. SOX trades at about a 2x forward P/E discount to the S&P 500, near the widest in 15 years.

Flows: desk activity was 6 on a 1-10 scale, finishing +2% better to buy. Asset managers and hedge funds were roughly balanced. Bartlett: the election outcome favors owners of compute (hyperscalers) and hurts those who build out, sell into or power data centers (neoclouds, semis, power). Several large buyers of Hyperscalers/Megas ex-semis and several large sellers of Semis/Datacenter plays.
Oil is at 1-month lows and 30yr and 10yr yields are back to mid-September levels. GS Econ expects data center moratoria to fade in importance and not be long-lived if enacted.

Shares were down about 4% pre-market after the earnings print underwhelmed.

sector_views.rationale: Desk flow shows large sellers of Semis and data center plays after the election. Multiples compressed from 28x to 16x forward P/E in two months.
Desk flow shows several large buyers of Hyperscalers and Megas ex-semis. The election backdrop is seen as good for owners of compute.
Retail rallied 5.5% in a day and XLP is at all-time highs, but the desk sees a lack of conviction and no aggressive single-stock buying.

earnings_insights: QCOM reported earnings that underwhelmed, with shares down about 9% pre-market on 11/5. The report gives no EPS or revenue figures.
ARM reported earnings that underwhelmed, with shares down about 4% pre-market on 11/5. The report gives no EPS or revenue figures.

Earnings before the open on 11/5 include AAP, APD, CI, CMI, COP, KMB, PH, RL, SO, TPR and ZTS, among others. Earnings after the close include ABNB, AXON, DKNG, DVN, EOG, LYFT, LYV, MCHP, MNST, NET, SPG and WYNN, among others.
VEEV holds an Investor Day on 11/5.

risk_factors: Further semis and data center weakness if the post-election rotation continues beyond the first day.
Market may over-price policy outcomes, especially if moves continue (CSPs > Semis, drawdowns in IPPs or E&Cs, sharp rally in consumer discretionary).
The consumer rally lacks conviction, and the ETF highs look macro and rotational rather than driven by single-name buying.
Oil rebound after a 14% weekly drop would pressure the consumer and rates narrative.
Treasury bill price sensitivity is rising amid sluggish MMF AUM growth.

tension_points.bull_case: GS Macro's 'Resilience' dashboard forecasts near-potential spending growth and real income acceleration in 2027, XRT is at 5-year highs and XLP at all-time highs, with lower oil and possible easing of SNAP and Medicaid headwinds in mid-2027.

tension_points.what_invalidates: A rebound in oil after the 14% weekly drop, or the rally continuing only through rotation without single-stock buying by the PB and high-touch desks.

tension_points.bear_case: Semis trade further below their 200-day moving average, with large desk sellers of Semis and Datacenter plays and the election backdrop seen as bad for those who build out, sell into or power data centers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Semis moves continuing beyond the first day would show whether the market is over-pricing policy outcomes.
